title: Exact inflation and invariants for product profinite condensed-group actions
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups (compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological groups), and write $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$, $\underline H(S)=C(S,H)$ for their condensed groups. For $P=1,G,H,G\times H$, let $\mathcal A_P(R)$ be the category of internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on this site equipped with an $R$-linear action $\underline P\times M\to M$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities, and equivariant $R$-linear morphisms. A linear action here means a family of module automorphisms parametrized by $\underline P$, or equivalently an action map additive and $R$-linear in the module variable. The trivial group gives ordinary internal $R$-modules.

These categories are Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For the projections $G\to1$, $H\to1$ and $G\times H\to G$, inflation (give the kernel trivial action without changing the module or maps) is additive and exact and has the invariants under that kernel as additive right adjoint. Invariants are the submodule of sections fixed after every profinite base change: $m\in M(S)$ is invariant if for every $T\to S$ and $g\in C(T,\ker)$, $g\cdot m|_T=m|_T$. For $G\times H\to G$ this retains the induced $G$-action. The adjunction bijection sends a map from an inflated module to its same map with codomain restricted to invariants; its inverse composes the invariant-submodule inclusion. The inflation from $\mathcal A_1(R)$ to $\mathcal A_{G\times H}(R)$ is the composite of inflation to $G$ and then along $G\times H\to G$, and the conjugate right-adjoint comparison is the identity identification
$$M^{G\times H}=(M^H)^G.$$
These assertions include either group trivial and the zero ring. They concern actions of condensed groups, rather than actions of the abstract group on a discrete module.

The trivial-group action category is equivalent to the original internal-module category by forgetting its unique action, so the latter is Grothendieck as well.

proof.text: The kernel/cokernel creation of lem-sfb-condensed-group-algebra-exact-forgetful implies that forgetting an action preserves finite limits and colimits. An inverse to an equivariant isomorphism of underlying modules is equivariant by cancellation, so forgetting reflects isomorphisms and hence finite limits and colimits. Trivial inflation and projection inflation commute strictly with forgetting and retain addition. Thus both inflations preserve finite limits and colimits.

proof.text: Restrict a product action to H and take the normalized invariants supplied by the coherent presentation. The action of (g,1) preserves these fixed sections: after any base change it commutes with (1,h). The invariant inclusion is injective, so each such image has a unique lift; lift addition, scalar multiplication, unit, multiplication and restriction identities through this inclusion. Equivariant maps restrict naturally, giving the additive residual G-action functor. The section-module functor of def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence makes the invariant inclusion linear for scalar multiplication.

proof.text: For an equivariant map out of first-projection inflation, its underlying map is H-equivariant from a trivial action. The normalized H-invariant adjunction restricts its codomain and retains G-equivariance, as checked through the inclusion. Conversely compose a G-equivariant map to H-invariants with the inclusion; equivariance for (g,h) follows from (g,h)=(g,1)(1,h). The normalized single-factor transpose formulas prove inverse and natural Hom bijections, and hence the product adjunction with its stipulated inclusions and fixed-section images.

proof.text: Direct trivial inflation equals the composite by the functor definitions. The normalized inverse transposes identify each adjunction counit with its invariant inclusion. Apply conjugateEquiv_counit to the equality isomorphism and evaluate on every profinite section. The composite counit is the two inclusions, giving precisely the required section identity. No step assumes a nontrivial group, a nonempty parameter, or nonzero coefficients.
